title: Vikings Flag WRs Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison as Questionable – ESPN Update
body:
The Minnesota Vikings entered Sunday’s showdown with the New Orleans Saints on shaky footing, as both of their premier wide receivers – Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison – were listed as questionable after injuries sustained in the week leading up to the game. Jefferson, who has been a catalyst for the Vikings’ explosive offense, suffered an ankle sprain, while Addison is nursing a hamstring strain that limited his practice reps. Their uncertain status left head coach Kevin O’Connell juggling line‑up decisions and forced the team to consider contingency plans for a matchup that could have significant playoff implications.

Jefferson’s ankle injury was first reported after he missed the final series of the Vikings’ Thursday night victory over the Chicago Bears. The 6‑foot‑4, 215‑pound playmaker has already posted more than 1,300 receiving yards this season, making him the league’s most productive receiver and a focal point of the Vikings’ passing attack. Even a minor limitation could hamper his ability to create separation and gain the yards after catch that have become his trademark. Medical staff indicated the sprain is moderate, and while there are no signs of a fracture, the decision will hinge on his ability to bear weight during the pre‑game warm‑up.

Addison, the former Penn State standout drafted in the first round, has been a rising secondary threat, tallying 45 receptions for 620 yards and three touchdowns in just 10 games. The hamstring strain was diagnosed after he slipped on the turf during a routine drill on Friday, prompting immediate evaluation. Hamstring injuries are notoriously fickle; a player can feel fine one day and be sidelined the next if the muscle fibers are overstressed. The Vikings’ trainers will monitor his range of motion and pain levels closely, but they have not ruled him out entirely.

The potential loss of both receivers not only threatens the Vikings’ aerial game plan but also puts additional pressure on the offensive line, particularly right tackle Riley Reiff, who was also listed as questionable after a lower‑body injury. Reiff’s role in protecting quarterback Kirk Cousins is critical against a Saints defense that has improved its pass rush in recent weeks. If Reiff is limited, Cousins could face increased pressure, forcing the offense to rely more heavily on short passes and the running game, where running back Alexander Mattison has been productive but still needs a spark to keep defenses honest.

Opponents will undoubtedly look to exploit the Vikings’ weakened receiving corps. New Orleans defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has emphasized scheming to disrupt the timing of the Vikings’ routes, and the Saints’ secondary has shown an ability to tighten coverage when key weapons are absent. However, Minnesota’s depth chart offers some reassurance. Veteran wideout K.J. Osborne, who has demonstrated reliable hands in clutch moments, could see an expanded role, while rookie tight end Irv Smith Jr. may be tasked with more short‑route duties to bridge the gap. Moreover, the Vikings’ offensive coordinator Wes Phillips has a reputation for creative play-calling that can adapt to personnel constraints, potentially incorporating more motion and jet sweeps to free up the remaining playmakers.

The outcome of this game could reverberate through the NFC North race. A win would keep the Vikings within striking distance of the Packers for the division lead, while a loss could widen the gap and force them into a must‑win scenario in their final two contests. Regardless of the health reports, the Vikings will need to execute a balanced attack, lean on their running backs, and trust in the depth of their receiving unit to stay competitive. As the team prepares for kickoff, the lingering question remains: can Minnesota’s offense adapt quickly enough to offset the potential absence of its two brightest stars and still secure a victory on the road?
